open_obligations: Check whether Choi et al.'s agents are samples from one model and, if so, whether correlated errors among them violate the independence assumption.
Note that Goel et al.'s passage concerns similarity across models; check whether it applies to repeated samples from one model.
Check Choi et al.'s condition that the correct answer is the most probable option.
in.other_title: Correlated failures risk: deferring to AI oversight as model blind spots converge
in.rationale: Choi, Zhu and Li prove majority voting succeeds with probability approaching 1 as N grows, assuming homogeneous independent agents whose top belief is on the correct answer. Goel et al. say that as model blind-spots get harder to detect, models also make more similar mistakes, and that if this trend continues it could undermine benefits from using LM juries by compromising independence; Goel et al.'s passage concerns similar mistakes across models, while Choi et al.'s agents share homogeneous initial beliefs, so the challenge is to the independence assumption in practice.
in.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether adding more LLM voters reliably drives majority-vote accuracy toward 1

open_obligations: Note that Liang et al.'s debate differs from majority voting over N independent agents.
Check the independence assumption and the Dirichlet belief model against real LLM agents.
Check whether more agents help when the correct answer is not the modal one.
out.other_title: Future work: more agents, board games, AI feedback for alignment
out.rationale: Both records concern using more agents. Liang et al. list scheduling more agents in the debate in an appropriate manner as future work. Choi, Zhu and Li prove that for N agents that respond independently without interaction, with homogeneous initial beliefs alpha in which the correct answer has the largest belief, majority voting picks the correct answer with probability at least 1 - exp(-N (Delta/sqrt(K) - 1/sqrt(N))^2) when N > K/Delta^2, where Delta is the margin theta-bar_1 - theta-bar_2 of the mean of Dirichlet(alpha). This is a result about independent voters in a Dirichlet belief model, not about measured LLM behaviour or agents in a debate, and it says nothing about how to schedule agents in a debate, while Liang et al.'s item makes no claim about voting, so neither bears on the other's claim.
out.scope: proposed SHARES_TOPIC: the number of agents in multi-agent LLM decisions, in Liang et al.'s debate and in Choi, Zhu and Li's majority voting over independent agents in a Dirichlet belief model

text: The authors state Theorem 1 (Majority Voting Success Probability): with theta-bar the mean of the Dirichlet distribution over K options and the margin Delta := theta-bar_1 - theta-bar_2, if N > K/Delta^2 then majority voting selects answer 1 with probability at least 1 - exp(-N (Delta/sqrt(K) - 1/sqrt(N))^2).
title: Majority voting success probability approaches 1 as the number of agents grows
